source: EMA / BCA Green Mark data, except Data Centre — see its own 'note' field for sources and revision date. Hospitality, Office/Professional Services, Retail (default) and Healthcare corrected 2026-09-27 against BCA's own primary-source Building Energy Benchmarks spreadsheet (go.gov.sg/bca-bebr-data, 'Building Energy Benchmarks' sheet, 2024 data) — see per-sector 'note' fields for the exact mapping and sample sizes. Manufacturing, F&B and Logistics are not covered by BEBR (a commercial/institutional-building dataset, not industrial) and are unchanged.

Hospitality.note: Corrected 2026-09-27 from an unsourced 200/350/550 band. BCA's 2024 Building Energy Benchmarks primary-source spreadsheet (go.gov.sg/bca-bebr-data), 'Hotel Buildings' row, n=79: top-quartile threshold <=200, median (2nd/3rd quartile boundary) 245, bottom-quartile threshold 311. bestInClass = top-quartile threshold, average = median, poor = bottom-quartile threshold (a prior WebSearch-only research pass could not resolve conflicting secondary summaries for this figure; this pass went to BCA's own primary spreadsheet instead).

default.note: Corrected 2026-09-27 from an unsourced 250/400/600 band. BCA's 2024 Building Energy Benchmarks primary-source spreadsheet (go.gov.sg/bca-bebr-data), 'Retail Buildings' row, n=114: top-quartile threshold <=244, median (2nd/3rd quartile boundary) 454, bottom-quartile threshold 536. bestInClass = top-quartile threshold, average = median, poor = bottom-quartile threshold. Real Singapore retail runs meaningfully more energy-intensive at the average/poor end than the prior placeholder assumed — driven mostly by refrigeration and long operating hours, per the same dynamic the 'supermarket' sub-profile below was already added to capture.

supermarket.note: Added so a supermarket/grocery client is no longer benchmarked against general-merchandise retail (usability finding M2 — a refrigeration-heavy store always looked 'worst quartile' otherwise). Derived from US EIA CBECS-style supermarket EUI of 40-60 kWh/sq ft/year (~430-645 kWh/m2/year), converted and centred; no Singapore-specific supermarket study was found. Refrigeration is ~50% of a supermarket's load. Source: apollo.eco 'Energy Use Intensity: Top Retail and F&B Benchmarks', LSBU 'Benchmarking of supermarket energy consumption'.

Office/Professional Services.note: Corrected 2026-09-27 from an unsourced 120/200/350 band. BCA's 2024 Building Energy Benchmarks primary-source spreadsheet (go.gov.sg/bca-bebr-data), 'Office Buildings' row, n=228: top-quartile threshold <=111, median (2nd/3rd quartile boundary) 144, bottom-quartile threshold 182. bestInClass = top-quartile threshold, average = median, poor = bottom-quartile threshold. The prior band overstated both average and poor substantially (200 and 350 vs. the real 144 and 182) — a typical Singapore office was being benchmarked as more efficient than it actually is relative to its peers.

Healthcare.note: Corrected 2026-09-27 from an unsourced 300/500/750 band. BCA's 2024 Building Energy Benchmarks primary-source spreadsheet (go.gov.sg/bca-bebr-data), 'Hospitals or Specialist Clinic' row, n=21: top-quartile threshold <=250, median (2nd/3rd quartile boundary) 305, bottom-quartile threshold 354. bestInClass = top-quartile threshold, average = median, poor = bottom-quartile threshold. BEBR separately reports Nursing Home (n=42) and Polyclinic/Private Clinic (n=12) bands, both materially lower than hospitals; this sector uses the hospital/specialist-clinic band as the more representative default for a generic 'Healthcare' classification, not a nursing home or polyclinic specifically.

coldStorage.note: Added so a cold-chain/reefer warehouse is no longer benchmarked against ambient logistics (usability finding M2). US DOE/industry data shows refrigerated warehouses run roughly 4-9x an ambient warehouse's electricity intensity (median ~25-31 kWh/sq ft/year, ~270-335 kWh/m2/year, refrigeration ~60-70% of load); no Singapore-specific cold-store study was found. Source: Mid-American Energy 'Save energy and money at your refrigerated warehouse'; Cold Chain Innovation Hub research.

Data Centre.note: Revised from a static 1.2/1.5/2.0 band to track Singapore's regulatory trajectory: PUE <=1.3 was already required for data centre capacity awarded in 2023, and <=1.25 for capacity awarded in Aug 2026, under the Green Data Centre Roadmap (May 2024) and energy-efficiency standard (Jun 2025). The Digital Infrastructure Act, which would make these thresholds legally enforceable across all operators (not just new capacity awards), was in public consultation Jul 2026 and is not yet finalized law as of this data's lastUpdated date — treat 'poor' (1.7, representative of pre-roadmap legacy facilities, which commonly ran 1.7-1.8) as 'not yet compliant with the direction of travel' rather than merely suboptimal. Sources: AKCP 'Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap: PUE 1.3 Ahead, and 1.25 for New Capacity' (2026); MDDI/IMDA Digital Infrastructure Bill public consultation, Jul 2026.
